Why do we talk about 10,000 steps a day? And what actually happens inside your body when you walk regularly?
The 10,000-step target became popular in Japan in the 1960s as part of the marketing of a pedometer called manpo-kei, or “10,000-step meter.” The number itself is not magical. What matters most is becoming consistently active and improving your fitness.
In this video, you will learn how regular walking can support:
• Muscle strength and endurance in the legs, hips, feet and core
• Blood sugar and glucose management through increased muscle activity
• Heart and blood-vessel health
